Load penetration test on RS soil (Red Crushed Volcanic Scoria (narrowly graded)) at relative density approx 0.0; apparatus: LPT fixture; loading: static penetration. Recorded: load vs penetration. One of 3 tests drawn from the same figures.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 24 of the 27 points, and the rest were settled against the scan. Student reviewers have looked at 8 of the 27 points on the scan; two reviewers confirmed 5 of them (see the provenance page). The test setup is incomplete: bin or mold, fill depth, rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![load against penetration, SI units, this test in red and the other tests printed in Fig. 2-32 in gray. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-lpt-053.png){.lightbox}

Peak load 217.6 N at 180.52 mm penetration, the end of the record.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-lpt-053/observations.csv) (27 points: 0 plotted symbols, 23 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1: load in N against penetration in m; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-lpt-053/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 603 micrometers in penetration, 1.313 N in load (0.6 percent of the peak). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 24 of the 27 points; the other 3 were settled against the scan (read by one reader and verified by the other, or decided between two readings). [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-f2-32).
